headline: Chinese scientists say they have solved a 30-year-old maths problem, the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture, with a Chinese AI model and human guidance.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a claimed proof of a long-open problem, but it rests on the lab's announcement and a preprint.
summary: IT Home, a Chinese technology news site, reports that the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory announced on 15 Oct 2026 a proof of the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture, a question about certain mathematical systems that Étienne Ghys, a French mathematician who is now a perpetual secretary of France's Academy of Sciences, posed in 1995. A team led by Xu Disheng, professor at Greater Bay Area University, used the lab's Shuwen-S2 model together with human experts, and a Peking University team says its SHEAF framework checked the proof by computer; the paper is a preprint on arXiv, so it has not been through peer review.
importance_line: Mathematicians in this field and AI labs gain a new claimed case of AI helping with research-level maths, but the result is the lab's own claim and still needs outside confirmation.
notes: KuCoin republishes IT Home; IT Home is credited as the reporter. Everything is the laboratory's own claim; no independent mathematician is quoted.
